title: Sundown output bisect notes
content:
Purpose: quick, messy bisect notes from tonight's sundown sampling. Not a polished report — scratchpad for next steps and handoffs.

Context:
- Regression noticed in production routing (~2024-10-31) where long-context chat responses became shorter and occasionally contradictory after model promos.
- Affected route: /v1/chat/generate default model redwood-v2-medium-8bit and fallback redwood-v2-medium-4bit.
- Symptoms: truncated reasoning near turn 3-5, weird drop in named-entity persistence across turns (previously stable).

Hypotheses (ranked quick):
1) KV cache packing change in serving runtime caused premature evictions for sequences > 1024 tokens. (most likely)
2) Subtle tokenizer change in model conversion pipeline — special token mapping altered, reduces prefix matching.
3) Quantization profile (8bit->4bit fallback) introduced accuracy cliff for rare tokens used in entity mentions.
4) Request routing now hitting a different kernel selection on newer hosts causing consistency differences.

What I ran (commands omitted — logs on PR1186):
- Sampled 300 production-like sessions (seeded), stratified by total tokens: short (<512), medium (512-1536), long (>1536).
- Compared outputs across three binaries: runtime@feat/kv-pack, runtime@main (Nov build), runtime@hotfix-eviction.

Representative sample (prompt redacted to keep PII out):
PROMPT (session 20124, turn 4):
"""
System: You are a helpful assistant. Keep state of named items across turns.
User: I mentioned my project 'BlueFjord' earlier; remind me what the team decided about the launch timeline and two dependencies.
"""

OUTPUT — runtime@main (post-promo):
A) "BlueFjord launch in Q4; dependencies: infra scaling, legal sign-off."
(Short. Misses the detailed dependency about 'billing migration' mentioned earlier.)

OUTPUT — runtime@feat/kv-pack (pre-promo):
B) "We planned a phased rollout: internal beta mid-September, public launch late Q4. Dependencies: infra scaling (autoscaler), billing migration (legacy->new), legal sign-off (privacy review)."
(Richer memory of earlier mention.)

OUTPUT — runtime@hotfix-eviction (this evening):
C) "Launch Q4; dependencies: autoscaler, privacy review."
(Also short; similar to runtime@main.)

Quick observations:
- feat/kv-pack preserves multi-turn state (B). Both main and hotfix collapse items — consistent with eviction or prefix mismatch.
- The missing token appears in the model inputs at index ~14k of aggregated session tokens (so not an early-token problem).
- No obvious detokenization errors in logs; token counts match expectations.
- Hotfix-eviction build did intentionally change some cache GC thresholds to mitigate memory pressure.

Ad-hoc rubric used for quick scoring (1-5, 5 best):
- State preservation: feat/kv-pack=5, main=2, hotfix=2
- Hallucination (false facts): feat/kv-pack=1, main=2, hotfix=2
- Verbosity/recall: feat/kv-pack=5, main=3, hotfix=2
- Safety: all 5 (not relevant here)

Immediate hypotheses to test next run (next-night):
- Reproduce by forcing same token-level inputs into a local runner with main vs feat/kv-pack and measure KV cache hits/misses per layer.
- Add debug dump of per-layer KV size and last-access timestamps to see if eviction is based on count or time.
- Run tokenizer diff between model-conversion artifacts to ensure no mapping changes.
- Run quant-sensitivity check: re-run session on 16-bit and 8-bit to see divergence point.

Notes to self / handoff points for SRE and runtime owners:
- SRE: can we temporarily pin routing for the affected customer to nodes running feat/kv-pack variant while we bisect? Need to know cost of maintaining pinning for ~48h.
- Runtime owners (@ravi): PR1186 touches GC thresholds — add a toggle and roll back quickly. Also add per-session metrics for last-kv-access.
- Applied-ML: please run a tokenizer mapping diff between model artifacts v2.1.3 and v2.2.0 and paste output here.

Quick TODOs (assignments in parentheses):
- Add KV-access debug instrumentation and re-run short test harness (Ines).
- Prepare a 30-min call with SRE + runtime owners tomorrow (Ravi).
- Create a small eval that seeds session with the rare token (Marta).
- If reproduced, prepare rollback plan for promo (Ines + Ravi).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why do both main and hotfix show same collapse pattern despite hotfix explicitly touching eviction thresholds? Maybe we introduced another change in the same promo cycle.
- Is there any correlation to host kernel selection? Need trace ids from production for the affected requests.

Quick pointers to logs (for handoff):
- Prod trace sample ids: trace-20241031-1A9, trace-20241031-1A12 (see linked slack thread).
- PR reference: runtime PR #1186 (debug in feature branch).

Finish: this is messy. Priority is to instrument KV last-access per-session and reproduce locally. If you pick this up, start with the 'medium' bucket — failures are highest there and faster to iterate.

-- Ines

(If anything here is stale by the time you read it: start from PR1186 and the prod traces listed above.)
